Problem 538. Classifying climate data: Station C
Knowledge context.
Climate descriptions summarize long-term patterns. In a reasoning problem, explicit thresholds let us classify numerical data without hidden knowledge.
Given facts.

Use this classroom classification: cool if mean temperature <12°C; mild if 12–17°C; warm if >17°C. Dry if annual precipitation <500 mm; wet if ≥500 mm. Data: Station A: T=10°C, P=490 mm; Station B: T=18°C, P=760 mm; Station C: T=14°C, P=540 mm.
Rules.
Apply only the stated thresholds. Temperature and precipitation are separate dimensions, so each station receives two labels.
Task.
Classify Station C. Then identify whether any other station has the same two-label class.
Step-by-step solution.
1. Compare T=14 with the temperature thresholds: it is mild. 2. Compare P=540 with 500 mm: it is wet. 3. Compare the combined label with the other stations; matches: none.
Answer.
Station C is mild and wet; no other station has the same class.
Knowledge takeaway.
Classification is the application of clear predicates to data; the rule must be stated before the label is inferred.
Formal model.
Numeric predicates with thresholds; output the conjunction of the temperature and precipitation categories.
